da-non-sequitur.evidence: CRITICAL: S↔P: the displayed dual is not the dual of this primal. x is free (md:5), so stationarity gives the equality y_0 + Σ_i G_ji y_i + s_j = t_j. The md writes "y_0 + Σ G_ji y_i − s_j ≤ t_j" (md:69) and the effective dual "y_0 + Σ G_ji y_i ≤ t_j" (md:86), which is the dual of the x ≥ 0 program. Exact counterexample (sympy, H_3, convention D, q = 11/10, n_target = 1; a weak-duality violation). t = (1, 1331/2210, 1331/2210, 1771561/4884100, 1771561/4884100, 32797171/48841000). The radical vector v = (−q³, q², q², −q, −q, 1) gives the primal-feasible x = (1331, −1210, −1210, 1100, 1100, −1000)/111: Σx = 1, Gx = 0, x ≥ −M for M ≥ 1210/111, objective 0. Meanwhile y = 0, s = 0, y_0 = 1771561/4884100 is feasible for both displayed duals with value > 0. Dual > primal, so the "strong duality" display (md:95-98) and "the dual certificate (y_0*, y*) certifies optimality" (md:26) are false as written. The prf proves strong duality only abstractly (prf:7-9) and never derives the dual. The prf also contradicts the statement's degeneracy section: "the Borromean link B_3 as the unique LP vertex" (prf:41-42) against md:49-56 "The set of minimisers is not a point". The active set {σ_0, L_-} (prf:37) is read off the non-optimal NF(B_3).

da-non-sequitur.evidence: Full review 2026-11-21. The statement block (operator-selection-lp.md) was repaired: the dual is now derived with equality constraints y_0 + sum_i G_ij y_i + w_j = t_j (md:70-90), the x>=0 inequality form is explicitly rejected, and a degeneracy section proves the optimum is 0 (G_1j = t_j) and the minimiser set is a face, not a point. The proof no longer claims 'B_3 as the unique LP vertex' and the active set read off NF(B_3) is gone, so the earlier critical findings (weak-duality counterexample at H_3, q=11/10; vertex-uniqueness contradiction) no longer apply. The prf's argument - non-empty, bounded (Sum x = n_target with x_i >= -M bounds every x_i above), hence LP strong duality - is valid. Remaining gaps: (1) prf:3-6 asserts G e_1 = t > 0 componentwise 'for generic q' without proof; feasibility needs t_j >= 0 for the rescaled identity, which is an archimedean sign claim on traces that is neither proved nor obviously true for all q; (2) the complementary-slackness display omits the box multipliers w_i(x_i + M) = 0; (3) the higher-strand table still lists d = n! before the box that corrects it to C_n, so the section reads as self-contradicting; the physical-regime column is interpretation, not used as a premise. No ruling conflicts.

trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR. VERIFIED CORRECT (all recomputed): d = n! = 2, 6, 24, 120 for n = 2..5; rank G = C_n = 2, 5, 14, 42 (Catalan); corank 0, 1, 10, 78 with the stated sum-of-squares decompositions exact — 10 = 3^2 + 1^2 is dim[2,1,1]^2 + dim[1^4]^2, and 78 = 6^2+5^2+4^2+1^2 is dim[3,1,1]^2 + dim[2,2,1]^2 + dim[2,1,1,1]^2 + dim[1^5]^2, i.e. exactly the l(lambda) >= 3 partitions the note says convention D kills; dim TL_n = C_n confirms the quotient claim. The tabled optimum sums to 0.998 - 0.010 + 0.009 + 0.046 - 0.044 + 0 = 0.999, consistent with the net constraint at n_target approx 1.000. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION (reported, not fixed): the n = 3 paragraph says 'the Borromean link B_3 as the unique LP vertex', and the sibling rem:operator-selection-lp-interpretation opens 'selects the Borromean link B_3 as the unique optimizer over the 6-element NF basis of H_3(q)' — but the correction blockquote FOUR LINES BELOW, in this same file, states that on H_n the LP 'has a corank G-dimensional space of optima differing by radical directions the trace cannot see', and it tabulates corank = 1 at n = 3. Uniqueness therefore holds only on the quotient H_3/rad tr_M = TL_3, not on the 6-element NF basis both sentences name. Proposed: qualify both 'unique' claims with 'on the quotient', or state the one-parameter radical family explicitly.
